statement: At T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 the cue's gain comes from self-checking deliberation (re-checks marked by 'Wait' / 'Hmm') that makes an answer robust to full-temperature sampling noise wherever in the answer it starts: the '\nOkay' opening is only the most common way into it, not a commitment made in the first few tokens, so plain answers that open tersely but later switch to self-checking recover most of the cued accuracy on the same problems.
why_strongest: It reproduces the three measured values. (1) D = 0.00: self-opened plain answers are in the self-checking register from the start, so on the same problems they are as robust at T 1.0 as cued answers. (2) R = 1.21: that register is long however it is entered, and a little longer without the cue's push. (3) AUROC 0.54: whether a sample opens with '\nOkay' is close to per-sample noise, because the opening is just one sampled entry point into the register and not a per-problem mode choice. It also fits the board. The plain base loses about 28-30 points from T 0.6 to T 1.0 on short problems and none on the longest (knowledge-9e4147). The cue is worth +7 to +12 points at T 0.6 but +37 at T 1.0 (result-7968b8, result-e870a1, result-c36598). Untruncated T 1.0 sampling hurts plain chain-of-thought (2407.01082). Self-checking words are the high-entropy forking tokens that carry reasoning (2506.01939), and the base already uses them (2503.20783, 2504.20571), so it does not need the opening to reach them. The theory and its advocate say the mode is fixed at the opening and 'nothing after the opening adds', so a terse opening means plain-mode accuracy (about 0.26-0.35 at T 1.0). The rival says the register is reachable at any point: what counts is whether the answer self-checks, not how it opens. The two accounts give the same numbers on every test so far, because each of those tests split answers only by their opening.

tests.experiment: On MATH-500 at T 1.0, plain base answers that do not self-open but contain a self-check marker later ('Wait' or 'Hmm'): their accuracy minus cued base accuracy on the same problems.
tests.recipe: Files: S3 T3.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl; base, plain, T 1.0) and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. If T3 holds more than one row for a problem_index, keep the first in file order. Score each kept T3 row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) from its text and gold. A cap_hit row keeps whatever score v3 gives, and an empty extraction counts 0. A T3 row is self-opened if the first 60 characters of its text field contain the substring '\nOkay' (newline immediately followed by 'Okay'). Let L = the problem_index values of T3 rows that are not self-opened and whose full text field contains the case-sensitive substring 'Wait' or the case-sensitive substring 'Hmm' (or both), restricted to problem_index values present in per_problem.json. A = mean v3 score of the T3 rows in L. B = mean of t1_right over the per_problem.json entries in L. Report A - B. If L is empty, report nothing.
tests.theory_should_say: The theory fixes the mode at the opening and says nothing after it adds, so these answers are plain mode: about 0.26-0.35 accurate against about 0.75-0.8 for cued answers on the same problems, a difference near -0.45. The rival says a later switch to self-checking restores most of the robustness, about -0.14.

tests.experiment: On MATH-500 at T 1.0, within the plain base answers that do not self-open: accuracy of those containing 'Wait' or 'Hmm' minus accuracy of those containing neither.
tests.recipe: File: S3 T3.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl; base, plain, T 1.0). If more than one row exists for a problem_index, keep the first in file order. Score each kept row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) from its text and gold. A cap_hit row keeps whatever score v3 gives, and an empty extraction counts 0. Drop rows that are self-opened (the first 60 characters of text contain the substring '\nOkay'). Among the remaining rows, group M = rows whose full text contains the case-sensitive substring 'Wait' or the case-sensitive substring 'Hmm'; group N = all other remaining rows. Report (mean v3 score of M) - (mean v3 score of N). If either group is empty, report nothing.
tests.theory_should_say: Both groups are the plain mode in the theory, since their opening is not '\nOkay' and later tokens add nothing, so the gap should be near 0 (or slightly negative, because answers that run long enough to say 'Wait' tend to be on harder problems). The rival gives a clearly positive gap of about +0.24.

tests.experiment: On the harder clean 328 at T 1.0, plain base answers that do not self-open but contain 'Wait' or 'Hmm': their accuracy minus cued base accuracy on the same problems.
tests.recipe: Files: S3 r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-132922-7ba0/answers.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-132922-7ba0/answers.jsonl; base, plain, T 1.0) and S3 r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base, cue, T 1.0). In each file, if more than one row exists for a problem_index, keep the row with the smallest attempt value (or, with no attempt field, the first in file order). Use the score_v3 column as the score; a null or missing score_v3 counts 0, and cap_hit rows keep their score_v3. A plain (7ba0) row is self-opened if the first 60 characters of its text field contain the substring '\nOkay'. Let L = the problem_index values whose kept 7ba0 row is not self-opened and whose full text contains the case-sensitive substring 'Wait' or the case-sensitive substring 'Hmm', and which also have a kept e72c row. A = mean score_v3 of the 7ba0 rows in L. B = mean score_v3 of the e72c rows in L. Report A - B. If L is empty, report nothing.
tests.theory_should_say: On the theory's mode account (extended to the harder set), terse-opened answers are plain mode (overall 76/328, about 0.23) against cued answers near 0.5, so the difference should be near -0.3. The rival says answers that switch to self-checking later are close to the cued ones, about -0.10.
